correctness.rationale: The two-red-register representation is equivalent to the original team split by downward closure. At most two mixed y-fibres can be covered; any three furnish a six-tuple failure. With two, exactly two assignments of red registers can cover both, and the resulting two Boolean failure clauses force precisely LL/RR four-tuple patterns or full-fibre-plus-cross-pair six-tuple patterns. With three, the types L,R,C have at most one L and one R in an inclusion-minimal failure. The weights t,t,2t yield exactly the stated formulas. The six-tuple witness in RESULT.md is deletion-minimal. Exhaustive reproducible diagnostics covered 1,450,240 finite subteams, with direct splitting checks on three domains; all passed. Neither finite tests nor status fields replace the general proof.

value.rationale: The number of values taken by the first determinant is a natural finite-domain parameter in dependence logic and database tables. This theorem exhibits a sharp qualitative boundary: a formula known incoherent without input restrictions has an exact six-tuple forbidden-obstruction bound with only a binary first determinant, plus a complete labelled two-size census and explicit local pattern classification for all two remaining alphabet sizes. The result gives a finite witness basis and computable benchmarks rather than an arbitrary numerical slice; no downstream theorem or publication-scale claim is presumed.
